stem: Measles is a highly infectious disease.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Name the pathogen that causes measles.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use the data in Fig. 6.1 to describe the pattern shown in the number of cases of measles reported to the WHO between January 2008 and December 2012.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The WHO is coordinating a vaccination campaign to reduce the number of cases of measles. Between seven to ten days after receiving the vaccination for measles the concentration of antibodies in the blood begins to increase.
parts.text: Describe what happens in the body after the injection of a measles vaccine until the concentration of antibodies in the blood begins to increase.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why countries that have established vaccination programmes still have cases of measles.
